reviewer.origin: Claude Agent tool subagent, model sonnet, a fresh context with only this brief and its files, launched 2026-10-26 by session_01Mxpoi6tFT3FgKmBvtGjRtS (the writer's session)

evidence: Read CONTEXT whole first (it is the same section text as G-S3a's, so it holds both the G-S3a pointer sentence and this draft). The draft sits mid-paragraph in 'Deciding to do it', after 'If you are going to use a recording, read the script if you can' and before 'You can also just open your eyes and stop': 'Remind yourself that if you say 'stop' at any time, the induction will end. If you say 'less', you will be asked to do less. If you say 'quiet', the talking will stop.' It appears once. AGAINST SOURCE: the two replaced sentences gave stop (the induction ends, at any time), less (it asks less of you) and quiet (the talking stops); the meaning-to-keep line gives the same three ('Stop' ends the exercise; 'less' reduces the demand; 'quiet' stops the words). The draft carries all three with the same effects. 'Remind yourself that' does the same job as 'Know that'; 'you can say' became a conditional that keeps the at-any-time availability; the dropped framing 'If you want to change something' is carried by the two effects themselves. It adds no fact, claim or step beyond the three controls the source already has, and the neighbouring sentences (open your eyes, no part has to approve) are untouched. It does what the_change says: three stop lines in place of the two sentences. VOICE AND SEAM: plain, short, repeated frames suit this paragraph and section, which already repeat frames ('Make it spacious? Make it warm and held?', 'Will you close your eyes? Will you come out...', 'Learn how to notice... Learn how to notice...') and which end by asking to keep the instructions about how to stay safe and how to get out plain. 'Also' in the next sentence follows from the list. I felt no seam. The only soft spots, both inherited from the replaced words, are the passive 'you will be asked' (by the narrator, who is named a paragraph later) and 'the talking will stop' sitting beside the command word 'stop'. TELLS: checked T01-T29 and C01-C04 on the literal draft in context. One row is PRESENT in form: T02 (three consecutive one-job conditions in a paragraph already built of short questions and rules). I do not accept the writer's ledger line that it is not part of a run. It is justified because these are three discrete controls the reader has to find and follow, the source states them in the same parallel form, the article itself asks for plain safety instructions, and the change adds one beat (two sentences became three) but no new job. Looked at and cleared: T12 (the three words are his three controls, not a package built for balance, and the stop line carries extra weight with 'at any time'); T09 and T13 (the neighbouring sentences about opening your eyes and about parts needing no permission are where this paragraph notices things); T20 and T29 (the third line is not the paragraph's end and states a control, not a moral); T22 and T10 (each line says what a word does, which is more than reassurance); T26 (stop and less recur as the controls' own words); T15 (plain words, no exotic swaps); C02 ('the induction' is named earlier in the section, and the asking and talking are the induction's, as in the replaced words). No other row PRESENT. LINTER: 'B7 short landing at paragraph end' is answered by the context: the line is the third of three controls and the paragraph goes on with two more sentences, so nothing lands at the end (the writer's reason also refers to 'Don't fake it', which belongs to another item). 'D9 follows the source order' holds because the three controls have no better order than the source's (stop, then less, then quiet); I do not rely on the writer's reason, which cites asides ('if I can put it that way', 'of course', 'just', '!') that are not in this draft; accepted on the context. 'E36/E41 heavy second person' (12.1 per 100): the four 'you' are the subject of three conditions and one passive in a how-to that addresses the reader throughout, and each 'you' says whose word triggers what; accepted. 'O30 you say three times': the repeat names three different words and what each does, in the plain parallel form the section asks for on exit instructions, and the frame is how the reader finds each control, so the repeat does the job; accepted. The author may still prefer a shorter frame, which is his call on the marking page.
